scientific_question: Does geometry-aware physical-space processing improve localization relative to a native-voxel implementation when model architecture, supervision, optimization, seeds, and evaluation are otherwise matched?

shared_training_contract.checkpoint_selection: maximum validation pFROC; exact ties retain earlier epoch

shared_intensity_contract.normalization_source: raw optimization-case intensity samples before spatial resampling

PHYSICAL.box_frame: patient-space physical coordinates with analytically transformed box corners

VOXEL.slice_order: same correct DICOM physical slice order as PHYSICAL; filename ordering is not permitted
VOXEL.spatial_preprocessing: no isotropic spacing normalization; operate on native voxel lattice
VOXEL.evaluation_conversion: predicted voxel boxes are transformed through the DICOM affine to the common physical evaluation frame before final metric computation

secondary_endpoints: median matched center error in millimetres

operating_point_for_secondary_endpoints.selection: fold-specific calibration partition; maximize sensitivity subject to FP/volume <= 1
operating_point_for_secondary_endpoints.outer_test_use: may be reported only as an explicitly post-lock exploratory secondary analysis because original outer-test outcomes were previously known

statistics.primary_test: two-sided exact sign-flip test on five fold-level mean pFROC differences after averaging five repeats within fold
statistics.case_level_uncertainty: 2000 case-level bootstrap replicates for any post-lock operating-point summary

cache_note: The existing 0.5-mm cache alone is insufficient to construct the native-voxel arm; raw DICOM or an equivalent native-grid cache is required.
failure_policy: retain and document every failure; implementation-only fixes are allowed before formal runs, but no performance-driven tuning
claim_rule: Do not claim that physical-space processing reduces scanner dependence unless the matched ablation supports the statement. If results are tied or negative, report that directly.
